caption: Newanforbi v. Candelaria, et al.
claims: Writ of Administrative Mandate (CCP §§1094.5, 473(d); Veh. Code §13559) — Set aside void APS Decision
status: NOT PURSUING — fee-payment deadline (~Jul. 27, 2026) lapsed without payment or a revised FW-001; Petitioner made the deliberate decision not to continue this petition given the burden of the retaliatory transfer to Santa Clara. The underlying CDL-suspension theory and its consequential damages remain live in the primary vehicle, Matter 7 (2:26-cv-00983-DC-CSK); this matter's equitable/vacatur track alone is abandoned.
note: Fee deadline lapsed ~Jul. 27, 2026 — not pursued further; Matter 7 remains the live vehicle for the same underlying theory.
defendants: Diana Candelaria, Driver Safety Hearing Officer, California DMV (official capacity); California Department of Motor Vehicles; Does 1-10
causes: Count I — Want of Statutory Predicate: No 'Lawful Arrest' (Veh. Code §13353(a)(1); CCP §1094.5(b)) — APS refusal suspension lacks 'lawful arrest' predicate; PC §849(b)(1) Detention Certificate (Nov. 5, 2024) irrevocably destroyed that predicate before the Jan. 24, 2025 hearing

Count II — Failure to Proceed in the Manner Required by Law (CCP §1094.5(b); Topanga Ass'n v. County of L.A., 11 Cal.3d 506) — Decision does not mention Detention Certificate; dismisses arguments as 'unpersuasive' without analysis; mischaracterizes record; never applies Mercer v. DMV or People v. Sanders

Count III — Findings Unsupported by the Weight of the Evidence (CCP §1094.5(c); Berlinghieri v. DMV, 33 Cal.3d 392) — Dashcam audio directly contradicts DS-367's 'strong distinct odor of alcohol'; only liquid identified on scene was urine; no objective signs of impairment on video; walk-and-turn abandoned by officers; no pass/fail FST standard

Count IV — Structural Bias — Unconstitutional Dual-Role Framework (U.S. Const. 14th Amend.; Cal. Const. art. I §7) — DMV hearing officer serves as both advocate and adjudicator; structural error under Knudsen v. DMV (no showing of actual prejudice required); framework condemned in Cal. DUI Lawyers Ass'n v. DMV, Knudsen, Clarke v. Gordon

Count V — Excess of Jurisdiction — Adjudication of a Non-Existent Subject Matter (CCP §1094.5(b)) — Decision void; rendered in clear absence of jurisdiction over subject matter that did not legally exist at time of hearing
key_facts: Verified Petition for Writ of Administrative Mandate challenging DMV APS Decision (Feb. 11, 2025, APS Case No. 34739340) suspending Class A CDL (License F7953179) for one year (Feb. 20, 2025 – Feb. 19, 2026). Central dispositive fact: Dublin CHP issued PC §849(b)(1) Detention Certificate (CHP Case No. RJ68845, Nov. 5, 2024) more than two months before the Jan. 24, 2025 APS hearing, certifying the Nov. 1, 2024 stop was 'a detention only, not an arrest.' APS jurisdiction under Veh. Code §13353(a)(1) is conditioned on a 'lawful arrest' — a predicate irrevocably destroyed by CHP's own agency-issued certificate before the hearing ever occurred. Respondent Candelaria's four-page Decision never once mentions the Detention Certificate and dismisses all petitioner's arguments as 'unpersuasive' without analysis. Dashcam transcript (00:54:36 – 01:57:10) shows: (1) liquid identified as urine, not alcohol, at 00:58:51 by Officer Melano ('This is piss'); (2) Officer Meza-Gonzalez declines to smell the cup; (3) no officer contemporaneously verbalizes alcohol odor in 62 minutes of recording; (4) walk-and-turn abandoned due to 'uneven ground'; (5) officers acknowledge no pass/fail FST standard (01:09:52); (6) PAS test expressly optional (01:10:54); (7) arrest ordered one second after lawful PAS refusal. DS-367 sworn claim of 'strong distinct odor of an alcoholic beverage' directly contradicted by dashcam. No accusatory pleading filed by Alameda County DA. Petitioner submitted five-page Personal Statement (Dec. 9, 2024) citing Terry v. Ohio, Mercer v. DMV, People v. Sanders, PC §§849(b)(1), 849(c), 849.5, 851.6(a). CDL suspension caused loss of commercial driving employment; CDL loss cited as aggravating factor in Nov. 2025 Discharge Review (Matter 9). Monetary consequential damages reserved for federal action (2:26-cv-00983-DC-CSK).
procedural_status: Verified Petition for Writ of Administrative Mandate electronically filed May 18, 2026, Sacramento Superior Court (Case No. 26WM000135; Deputy T. Mercadel). Trial by Court — No Jury. APS Case No. 34739340; DL/ID No. F7953179. Petitioner exhausted all administrative remedies: timely requested APS hearing; submitted five-page Personal Statement (Dec. 9, 2024); appeared Jan. 24, 2025; presented Detention Certificate, dashcam transcript, and binding authority. Respondent Candelaria's Decision (Feb. 11, 2025) is the final agency action. Petition claims Decision is void ab initio under CCP §473(d) — not subject to the ordinary 34-day limitations period of Veh. Code §13559(a). Attorney's fees sought under CCP §1021.5. Fee Waiver (FW-001): Request filed 05/18/2026 (concurrent with petition). 05/19/2026: Court issued Order on Court Fee Waiver (FW-003, signed by Judicial Officer, filed by E. Macdonald, Deputy) — DENIED under §4b: request incomplete (§4b(1)); and §4c(1) checked: court needs more information — 'Because Applicant checked Section 7 on Page 2 of Form FW-001 the Court needs to review Applicant's average monthly income going back 12 months or from April 2025 through April 2026.' Petitioner had 10 days from notice (mailed 05/20/2026 from Sacramento by Kelly Sullivan, Court Executive Officer, /s/ E. Macdonald) to pay fees/costs or file a revised FW-001 with 12-month income documentation. Fee Waiver Hearing: July 17, 2026, 9:00 AM, Dept. 10C, Tani G. Cantil-Sakauye Courthouse, 500 G Street, Sacramento, CA 95814— DID NOT GO FORWARD: Petitioner did not appear. On June 29, 2026 — 18 days before the hearing — CDCR ordered a retaliatory transfer of Petitioner's parole supervision from Stockton to the Santa Clara GPS Unit (see Matter 30, Newanforbi v. Moua, et al.), placing him too far from Sacramento to attend. Per the form's own instructions, non-appearance results in denial of the fee waiver and triggers a 10-day deadline to pay the filing fees/costs, running from July 17, 2026 (due on or about July 27, 2026). This is a direct, concrete downstream harm from the retaliatory transfer, independent of the harms already pled in Matter 30. July 27, 2026: the fee-payment deadline passed without payment and without a revised FW-001 being filed — a deliberate decision, not an oversight, given the burden the retaliatory transfer already placed on Petitioner's ability to litigate this matter from Santa Clara. The petition is not being pursued further and will lapse for non-payment. This does not affect Matter 7 (2:26-cv-00983-DC-CSK), the federal action asserting the same underlying structural-bias and CDL-suspension theory with money damages, which remains the primary live vehicle for this claim.
damages: Equitable: (a) set aside Decision in its entirety; (b) vacate one-year Class A CDL suspension (Feb. 20, 2025 – Feb. 19, 2026); (c) restore commercial driving privileges nunc pro tunc to Feb. 20, 2025; (d) vacate $125 reissue fee (Veh. Code §§14904, 14906); (e) vacate three-year SR-22 financial-responsibility requirement (Veh. Code §16430); (f) expunge all suspension notations from driving record; (g) refund $125 reissue fee with interest from date of payment. SR-22 insurance: Policy No. GPCP-00713747-00; $403.04 paid to date; $29.55/month; 3-year exposure ≥$1,340.04 (consequential damages reserved for federal action, 2:26-cv-00983-DC-CSK). Attorney's fees under CCP §1021.5.
risk: Favorable: Candelaria sued in official capacity only — no individual capacity immunity arguments. Detention Certificate is categorically dispositive: CHP's own agency issued PC §849(b)(1) certificate reclassifying event as 'detention only, not an arrest' more than two months before the Jan. 24, 2025 hearing. Under Knudsen structural error doctrine, no showing of actual prejudice is required. Decision's failure to mention Detention Certificate anywhere is the central due process violation. APS decision is void (not merely voidable) for want of subject-matter jurisdiction, which cannot be insulated by the 34-day limitations period of Veh. Code §13559(a). Independent judgment standard (Berlinghieri/Daniels) applies because CDL is a fundamental vested right and means of livelihood.
evidence: APS Notification of Findings and Decision (Feb. 11, 2025, APS Case 34739340) — signed D. Candelaria; four-page decision never once mentions Detention Certificate; dismisses all arguments as 'unpersuasive' without analysis; mischaracterizes record ('No evidence was presented to the contrary')

Dublin CHP Detention Certificate (CHP Case No. RJ68845, Nov. 5, 2024) — certifies taking into custody 'was a detention only, not an arrest'; released under PC §849(b)(1) for 'insufficient grounds for making a criminal complaint'; signed Officer Del Carlo L., Badge 022511

CHP Dashcam Transcript (Nov. 1, 2024, I-580 East Livermore, recording 00:54:36 – 01:57:10) — Melano confirms liquid is urine at 00:58:51 ('This is piss'); Meza-Gonzalez declines to smell cup at 00:59:02; Melano confirms 'piss everywhere' at 01:23:26; no officer contemporaneously verbalizes alcohol odor from Plaintiff's breath or person in 62 minutes; walk-and-turn abandoned due to 'uneven ground' (Melano); officers acknowledge no pass/fail standard for FSTs (01:09:52); PAS test expressly optional (01:10:54); arrest ordered one second after lawful PAS refusal

DS-367 (Officer Santiago Meza-Gonzalez, Badge #023295, Nov. 1, 2024) — sworn claim of 'strong distinct odor of an alcoholic beverage' directly contradicted by dashcam; PAS section blank; chemical test refusal checked; blood draw warrant WAR913372 obtained
CHP Arrest-Investigation Report (Case RJ68845, Meza-Gonzalez) — charges recommended: Veh. Code §§23152(a), 23152(b), 23578; no accusatory pleading filed by Alameda County DA

Notice of Response to Request for Discovery — Personal Statement (submitted Dec. 9, 2024) — five-page submission citing Terry v. Ohio, Mercer v. DMV, People v. Sanders, PC §§849(b)(1), 849(c), 849.5, 851.6(a)

DMV Notice of Hearing Appointment (Form DS 2304, Rev. 05/2023, Dec. 4, 2024) — sets Jan. 24, 2025 hearing via Microsoft Teams before Candelaria (Meeting ID 241846391884; Conf. ID 159660245); issued by C. Winston, Sacramento Driver Safety Office
